evals.name: gtd-weekly-review
evals.prompt: What are the exact steps of the GTD Weekly Review in David Allen's revised Getting Things Done?
assertions: Groups into Get Clear, Get Current, Get Creative
Get Clear: collect loose papers/materials, get 'in' to zero, empty your head
Get Current: review action lists, previous calendar, upcoming calendar
Get Current: review Waiting For, project lists, relevant checklists
Get Creative: review Someday/Maybe and be creative and courageous
Explains purpose: keeping the system current and trusted (reflect step)

evals.name: gtd-horizons
evals.prompt: Explain the GTD horizons of focus and the models Allen gives for choosing what to work on.
assertions: Lists Ground (current actions) through Horizon 5 (purpose and principles), including areas of focus (H2), goals (H3), vision (H4)
Four-criteria model in order: context, time available, energy available, priority
Threefold model: predefined work, work as it shows up, defining your work
Identifies the six-level model as the horizons used for reviewing work
Defines a project as any outcome achievable within a year requiring more than one action
Connects horizons to weekly review / top-down priorities

evals.name: gtd-inbox
evals.prompt: My inbox and head are overflowing. Walk me through processing everything the GTD way.
assertions: Capture everything first (mind sweep / collection buckets)
Clarify one item at a time asking What is it? Is it actionable?
Non-actionable: trash, incubate (someday/maybe or tickler), or reference
Actionable: decide next action; two-minute rule (do it if under two minutes); otherwise delegate (Waiting For) or defer (calendar or Next Actions)
Organize into the categories (projects, next actions by context, waiting for, calendar, reference, someday/maybe)
Mentions weekly review / reflect and engage to keep the system trusted
